physicalNotes: Radius 0.943 Jupiter radii from Yee et al. 2025 (2025ApJS..280...30Y), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..280...30Y/abstract): 67,417 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.312 Jupiter masses (Yee et al. 2025, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2025ApJS..280...30Y), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2025ApJS..280...30Y/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Yee et al. 2025 (2025ApJS..280...30Y), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname YEE_ET_AL_2025): P 2.21778105 d
sources.shape: Yee et al. 2025 (2025ApJS..280...30Y), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname YEE_ET_AL_2025): a/R* 8.57; Yee et al. 2025 (2025ApJS..280...30Y), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname YEE_ET_AL_2025): inclination 85.2 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Yee et al. 2025 (2025ApJS..280...30Y), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname YEE_ET_AL_2025): transit mid-time 2459797.24218 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 1 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
